newsitem.title: USA: Couple accused of beating Russian children on jet.
newsitem.headline: Couple accused of beating Russian children on jet.

text.p: A wealthy Arizona couple accused of beating two 4-year-old girls they had just adopted in Russia pleaded not guilty, officials said on Friday.

Richard Thorne, 48, and his wife, Karen, 42, of Phoenix, who were flying to New York from Moscow with the girls, were seen striking them several times in the stomach and chest by flight attendant Brenda Cruz and other passengers on the flight, the complaint filed in Queens Criminal Court says.

It alleges that the Thornes "repeatedly" beat the girls and "pulled their arms with extreme force" during the ten-hour flight. Cruz also observed the couple strike the children in the back of their legs, causing them to fall suddenly.
Karen Thorne "was screaming and shouting" at the children who "were crying and visibly displaying pain and cowering each time" her husband struck them, the complaint says.
Richard Thorne is alleged to have slapped the terrified girls and was heard "forcefully and repeatedly" shouting at them to "shut up or I'll send you back to Russia."

Passengers and crew members who witnessed the alleged abuse said the girls were struck "repeatedly about the head, face and body." Many of the passengers refused to be processed through customs until the Thornes were arrested, police said.
The Thornes are charged with two counts of endangering the welfare of a child, assault and harassment. They face up to a year in jail if convicted.
"Several passengers and crew members tried to stop the couple from smacking the children but they were rebuffed," Queens District Attorney spokeswoman Mary deBourbon said.

She said the couple went to Moscow on April 18 to pick up the girls, who are not related, at an orphanage. They were supposed to make a connecting flight from New York to Arizona when they were arrested on Wednesday after the pilot alerted police to meet the plane at John F. Kennedy airport.
The children, who suffered bruises, have been placed in foster care, Maggie Lear, a spokeswoman of the Administration for Children's Services, said.
Unable to post $5,000 bail, the couple are being held at the Rikers Island jail awaiting a June 11 hearing.
